P6.text: no OOM by 16K, standard fastest on prefill again unless the port materializes S x S on full layers (say which from the code before the card)
P6.status: CODE READING DONE BEFORE THE CARD, AND ALREADY REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT
P6.code_reading: The port DOES materialize S x S on full-attention layers. sink_attention_tc (gpt_oss20b_tc.py:345-372) computes scores = matmul(query, key_h) with NO chunking, giving a dense B x H x L x S tensor, then adds a full (1,1,L,S) mask, then tc.cat s an extra sink column (a SECOND S+1-wide tensor), then softmaxes. At H=64 that is 512 MiB per tensor at S=2048 and 2,048 MiB at S=4096.
P6.result: REFUTED on both halves. Standard OOMs at W=2048, far short of 16K. The APA arms, whose fused kernels are O(L) in score memory, DO fit 2048. This inverts Gemma and reproduces MiniCPM3: APA buys real memory headroom here.

S1.text: The per-call fp32 exactness gate PASSES on real activations at <= 1e-5 relF, exactly as the synthetic shape pin did. The sink adds no new exactness risk because it enters after every selection decision and is a single scalar per head — the same arithmetic in both paths.

S2.text: The model-level D-vs-A difference will be LARGE in absolute ppl (tens of points) and still NOT RESOLVABLE, because this model amplifies bf16 rounding even harder than Gemma did: the measured floor is 8.7 % of baseline vs Gemma's ~4.9 %. Already supported: D 657.55 vs A 673.12 at W=1024 window 0 is a 15.6 ppl / 2.3 % difference, comfortably inside 58.76.

S3.text: P4 MISSES: E refines ESSENTIALLY EVERYTHING (>= 95 %), like MiniCPM3 and unlike Gemma. Reason: the provable delta is set by the quantizer WORST CASE, and on these keys the max error (19.86) is 28x the mean (0.71) and 4x the p99 (4.90). delta = 44.3 will sit far above the running-max spread of almost every query. The Gemma result was a property of an unusually clean quantizer, not of the rule.

S4.text: C - B will be NEGATIVE in sign (C better) but the magnitude will be swamped by the floor, so P3 is HIT only in the weak sense of "inside the floor". Mechanism: the z-score tail leaves ~48 % of mass unrefined here vs 25 % on Gemma and 92 % on MiniCPM3, and the bulk keys are the noisiest of the three, so there IS something for the running-max tail to fix — just not 58 ppl worth of it.

S5.text: The 3 layers with near-zero sink mass (11: 1.3 %, 13: 1.3 %, 7: 6.7 %) and the 3 with very high sink mass (19: 64 %, 21: 58 %, 23: 40 %) will show DIFFERENT unrefined-mass behaviour, because a query that puts 64 % of its mass in the sink has only 36 % distributed over real keys and so a much flatter effective distribution over them. Specifically I predict the high-sink layers show HIGHER unrefined real-key mass at the same delta. This is the one thing no previous model in this series could be asked.
S5.confidence: medium — this is a genuine open question, not a restatement of a measurement

S6.text: On the ceiling: the APA arms reach 4096 and probably 8192 under the rail, and standard reaches NEITHER — standard's wall is memory at 2048 while the APA arms' wall will be TIME, not memory, because the resident MXFP4 body leaves only 927 MiB and the fused path's KV grows ~12 MiB per 1K tokens (8 KV heads x 64 dim x 2 tensors x 2 B x 24 layers). Extrapolating, KV alone reaches 927 MiB at roughly 75K tokens, so time rails first.
